newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on brisk sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on brisk sales.

text.p: Brisk selling from Japan in the morning and from Europe during afternoon trade drove Hong Kong gold further down on Wednesday, with spot prices ending below New York's Tuesday close, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$373.90/374.40 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$374.70/375.20 close on Tuesday.

Japanese traders were offering gold in yen during currency swings, market sources said. Numerous gold traders reported selling out of Europe in the afternoon, partiuclarly from London, but said they did not know the sellers' identity.
One bullion dealer at a market-making firm said central banks, particularly the Swiss, could be behind the selling, but this could not be confirmed.
"It's mainly speculative selling from people getting rid of positions ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday and the options expiry tonight," said an international bank dealer.
But gold was well supported at $374 per ounce, as physical demand perked up in Hong Kong on Wednesday, dealers said.
A senior trader earlier in the day discounted worries of central banks' gold sales, noting the overhang had always haunted the market.

Others worried more about producer selling, noting short term gold lease rates were inching up, with one month at 2.75 percent (on the Reuters GOFO page) pointing to increased demand with mines selling forward and needing to finance.
Local gold ended HK$4 lower at HK$3,453 a tael.
The Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil, from its previous fix at -3.00.
